title: W8 bundle-replication pin is vacuous for load columns: the record is read post-drain (tick 20) where both members report all-zero load
evidence:
test_stats_bundle_member_replication steps `for tick in u64(1)..=20 {` then computes ONE record after the loop and asserts:
```
		testing.expect_value(t, m0.cap_units, u32(30))
		testing.expect_value(t, m1.cap_units, u32(30))
		// identical load columns (the pooled link)
		testing.expect_value(t, m0.offered, m1.offered)
		testing.expect_value(t, m0.carried, m1.carried)
		testing.expect_value(t, m0.dropped, m1.dropped)
		testing.expect_value(t, m0.util_pct, m1.util_pct)
		testing.expect_value(t, m0.q, m1.q)
		// lane columns are per-pipe but the flow allocates the same default
		// preset to both (balanced 1:1:1) — the caps are identical here
		testing.expect(t, m0.w == m1.w, "default weights are per-pipe but identical")
		// the offered==carried+drops invariant holds for members too
		testing.expect(t, m0.offered == m0.carried + u64(m0.dropped) * 30, "member offered invariant")
```
Verified by replicating the exact test shape (seed 99, era 0, 2x Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a=r,b=g,tier=1} + g->h, 10 email seeds ticks 1..10) against the worktree core package: at the assertion point (after tick 20) both members read `m0[cap=30 off=0 car=0 dr=0 util=0 q=[0,0,0]] m1[cap=30 off=0 car=0 dr=0 util=0 q=[0,0,0]]` — every load-column equality is 0==0 and the member offered invariant is 0==0+0*30. At ticks 1..8 the same run's members carry identical NON-ZERO load `m0[cap=30 off=30 car=30 dr=0 util=100 q=[0,1,0]] m1[...]` (probe output), and harness `run bundle --stats-out` shows live member rows `P,57,1,...,30,30,30,0,100,...,0,1,0` / `P,57,2,...,30,30,30,0,100,...,0,1,0` — discriminating data exists mid-flight.
detail: The r2 claim 'W8 fixed: 2-member bundle replication pinned' is incomplete: only cap_units=30 discriminates (per-pipe read would give 15). A regression making members read per-pipe instead of bundle load keeps offered/carried/dropped/util/q equalities green (both zero).
recommended_fix: Compute the record at a mid-flight tick (e.g. tick 3, or per-tick in the loop) and assert m0/m1 load columns are identical AND non-zero (offered==30, util==100, q==[0,1,0]) — one-line change; mid-flight data verified present.

title: W6 D-row aggregation semantic (one row per (pipe,class,reason) with summed count) is unpinned — duplicate-row regressions stay green
detail: The r2 claim 'D rows aggregate per (pipe,class,reason)' is behaviorally true in code but unpinned: the documented stream format ('multiple same-kind sheds in one tick sum into one row — the count column is meaningful') can silently change shape with all tests and stats-check byte-compare green (both sides drift together).
recommended_fix: Add an assertion that no two rows in rec.drops share (pipe,class,reason) — e.g. a double loop asserting uniqueness — and/or pin the known tick-12 shape (one row, pipe 1, class 1, count 2).

title: App-side and harness CLI error paths for --stats-out (W1 exit 2, W2 exit 1, single-demo guard) have no automated coverage
detail: The spec's I/O matrix error rows (dangling flag, unwritable path, >1 demo) are exactly the r1 W1/W2 fixes, yet only manual verification covers them; a regression to silent telemetry-off would pass the suite.
recommended_fix: Add a harness-level test (or extend drift-check-style verb) asserting `run a b --stats-out x` and a dangling `--stats-out` exit 2; document the app paths as manual-checklist items in the PR body.

title: No literal pin of the CSV row format or the G-row field passthroughs (gen/score/meter) — format regressions pass byte-identity tests
evidence:
core/stats.odin serializer:
```
	fmt.sbprintf(sb, "G,%d,%d,%016x,%d,%d\n",
		rec.tick, rec.gen, rec.sim_hash, rec.score, rec.meter)
	for c in rec.classes {
		fmt.sbprintf(sb, "C,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d\n", ...
```
The only content-level assertions anywhere are substring checks in test_stats_emit_path (`strings.contains(out, fmt.tprintf("G,1,"))`, `strings.contains(out, "P,")`, `!strings.contains(out, "# pp stats stream")`); the byte-identity and replay-identity tests compare the serializer against itself. No test asserts a literal expected row (column order/count, %016x hash width) or expect_value on rec.gen/rec.score/rec.meter.
detail: A column swap (e.g. wE/wS) or a wrong G-row field copies identically into live and replay streams — all 164 tests, stats-check, and CI stay green while the documented format silently changes.
recommended_fix: Pin one literal row of each kind (e.g. the PR-body tick-21 excerpt as an expected-string test) and expect_value the G-row record fields (gen/score/meter) in test_stats_derivation_congested.
